blocks.label: Figure
blocks.text: What stands on the site today: what is kept, what is adapted and what is demolished.

blocks.heading: WHAT IS THERE NOW
paras: The port, cargo yards and warehouses hold 9.90 ha, 74% of the 13.43 ha area. They block the sea and fill the streets with trucks. Behind them, 9,230 people live on 2.53 ha of homes. The plan has to give this edge back to the city.

cards.title: A blocked waterfront
cards.text: Waterfront blocked by industrial and godown uses, limiting public access.

cards.title: No room to play
cards.text: High building density leaves little space for public recreation.

cards.title: Far from the bus
cards.text: Distant bus stops increase dependence on private vehicles.

cards.title: Pipes in the way
cards.text: Exposed roadside pipes obstruct pedestrian movement.

cards.title: A traffic barrier
cards.text: A busy road acts as a barrier.

cards.title: One strip for all
cards.text: Narrow roads force pedestrians and vehicles to share unsafe space.

blocks.heading: WHAT THE IMAGES SHOW
paras: On the ground, the edge feels closed. Warehouse walls stand where the sea should be, and buildings press close, with no room left for play. Narrow roads leave people and motorbikes to share one strip, and bus stops are far, so many people drive.
